Hi Julia — thanks for the flag and for the screenshot. I've opened an internal support case (SUP-8492) and looped in engineering and security to scope the removal steps.

Quick answers up front:
- We can remove the payload and model output for a single conversation from our request logs for hosted customers if we have the conversation/request ID and an authorized deletion request.
- Some derived/billing metadata (hashed ids, invoice line items) and immutable audit records used for compliance may persist in a limited form; I list specifics below.

Next steps we need from you:
1) A signed deletion authorization from an Acme authorized approver (screenshot + signature is not sufficient).
2) Confirmation of the exact conversation/request id to be purged (you listed conv-8492; please confirm REQ-20260305-8492).

I've attached our deletion request instructions (redwood-data-deletion-instructions.pdf) that describe timeline and what can/can't be removed. Dev, Olga — can you confirm the estimated turnaround and what will remain in audit/billing?

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Mar 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick answers up front:
> - We can remove the payload and model output for a single conversation from our request logs for hosted customers if we have the conversation/request ID and an authorized deletion request.

Thanks — confirming the technical scope here and the expected steps.

What we can remove (hosted API):
- Full request payload (user prompt) and full response text stored in request logs/telemetry for the specified conversation ID.
- Any cached KV/LLM session artifacts tied strictly to that conversation key.

What we cannot fully remove (for compliance/audit reasons):
- High-level billing records that indicate a request occurred (timestamp, cost bucket) — we retain hashed identifiers for 12 months for billing reconciliation.
- Immutable audit logs required by SOC-like controls (these keep an event entry but we can redact payloads).

Procedure:
1) Provide the signed deletion authorization PDF and confirm the precise conversation IDs (conv-8492 / REQ-20260305-8492).
2) We create a purge job scoped to those IDs and perform deletion from request logs and caches.
3) Security (Olga) will validate and approve before we run the job.
4) We provide a confirmation report (files removed, timestamps) and a support case link.

ETA: 3 business days after receiving the signed authorization and account ownership confirmation. If additional legal review is required for retention exceptions, add 3–5 business days.

I attached the deletion instructions as requested by Marissa.

—Dev

- Deleted: full request payload and model output from request logs; KV cache entries tied to the session; copies in telemetry aggregates were redacted.
- Retained (immutable/limited): billing event entries (timestamp + cost bucket), hashed request identifiers for 12 months, and audit event markers that indicate a purge occurred (no payload).
